title: GPU VRAM estimate scaled by wrong denominator (safe_row_limit instead of total_rows), overstating VRAM whenever RAM downsampling applies
description: The reactive `adjusted` memo rescales the backend's `gpu_vram_estimated_mb` to the user's effective GPU row count, but uses `originalRows = safe_row_limit ?? sourceRows` as the baseline the backend estimate was computed at. The backend actually computes that estimate at `total_rows` (full source rows), NOT at `safe_row_limit`. So whenever `was_downsampled` is true (i.e. `safe_row_limit < total_rows`), the displayed GPU VRAM is inflated by a factor of `sourceRows / safe_row_limit`. This also feeds the warning banner at lines 170-177 ("GPU training needs ~X but GPU has Y. Training will fall back to CPU automatically."), so a spurious CPU-fallback warning can be shown to the user even when the GPU could actually fit the workload.
evidence: Backend: src/haute/routes/modelling.py:196 sets `effective_rows = ram_est.total_rows or 0` and line 203 calls `_check_gpu_vram(effective_rows, ...)`, whose result populates `gpu_vram_estimated_mb` (line 218). So the baseline row count for the estimate is `total_rows == sourceRows`. Frontend TrainingActionsAndResults.tsx: line 76 `gpuRows = hasUserLimit ? Math.min(rowLimit, sourceRows) : sourceRows`; line 77 `originalRows = ramEstimate.safe_row_limit ?? sourceRows`; line 79 `gpuVramMb = gpuVramMb * gpuRows / originalRows`. Case: total_rows=100000, safe_row_limit=50000 (was_downsampled), no user rowLimit -> gpuRows=100000, originalRows=50000, gpuRows!==originalRows so it scales B*100000/50000 = 2*B, doubling the estimate the backend already computed for 100000 rows. With a user limit L: scales B*min(L,source)/safe_row_limit instead of the correct B*min(L,source)/sourceRows, still overstated by sourceRows/safe_row_limit. The correct denominator is `total_rows` (sourceRows). Not covered by TrainingActionsAndResults.test.tsx (no test sets gpu_vram_estimated_mb together with safe_row_limit).
